messages:
kelly_sales (Sales): Heads up — BankCorp sent a vendor risk pack and their SIG specifically calls out: BYOK, split custody, ability to decrypt historic records after rotation, and whether we ever hold plaintext keys. Need short, copy-pasteable answers + a pragmatic POC plan.

arap_se (SE): Quick tech notes I can turn into SIG responses: we use envelope encryption where each object is encrypted with a short-lived data key (AES-256-GCM). Data keys are wrapped by a master key (CMK) stored in a cloud KMS or customer HSM. Data keys are ephemeral in memory and never persisted unencrypted.

nina_sec (Security): Add controls: CMKs we integrate with are non-exportable by default. For customer-managed HSMs you can choose an import policy but our hosted offering never exports CMKs. We also maintain key operation audit trails (who/when/what) and integrate with SIEM exports.

omar_ae (AE): BankCorp asked about split custody options — can we support a model where Redwood cannot decrypt without a customer-held piece (quorum or dual-control)? They flagged regulatory need for separation of duties.

arap_se (SE): Yes — options: 1) Customer keeps CMKs in their KMS/HSM and we perform KMS calls (Redwood never holds key material). 2) For Dedicated/Private we can run an HSM connector inside the customer's VPC so key operations require the customer's HSM to authorize. 3) For very high-assurance workflows, we support a dual-control process: two approvals required to rotate/export key metadata (operational, not cryptographic split by default). We can discuss multi-party HSM providers if they insist on cryptographic splitting.

nina_sec (Security): Important to highlight: plaintext master key material is never persisted on Redwood systems. If a customer requests us to import key material into an on-prem HSM we follow a documented import workflow with custodial controls and audit.

arap_se (SE): Regarding rotation and historic decrypts: our default is key versioning + envelope rewrap on read. New writes use newest key version; older objects remain decryptable by referencing the key version ID stored with the object. We can optionally run a bulk rewrap to move all objects to a new key if customer policy requires it. Automation for scheduled rotation and rewrap is available in Dedicated/Private POCs.

omar_ae (AE): They want a short assurance blurb for their vendor review that we can paste into SIG/CAIQ.

nina_sec (Security): Suggested assurance text (one paragraph): "Redwood Inference uses envelope encryption with AES-256-GCM for data at rest; master keys (CMKs) are managed either by the customer or by a cloud/HSM-backed KMS. Redwood does not persist unencrypted key material. When integrated with customer-managed KMS/HSM, Redwood performs cryptographic operations via API calls — master keys remain under customer control and key usage is recorded in audit logs available for review."

arap_se (SE): POC steps (minimal): 1) Create staging tenant + enable KMS connector, 2) Run sign/encrypt/decrypt vectors and record audit logs, 3) Execute rotation cycle and validate older objects still decrypt, 4) Test failover where KMS is unreachable & observe error/fallback behavior. Estimate: 2-4 business days for engineering + security review.

arap_se (SE): Example connector registration (replace with their values):
```
POST https://kms-connector.redwood.internal/v1/attach
Authorization: Bearer <redwood-token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "provider": "aws",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "key_id": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234",
  "mtls_cert": "<base64-client-cert>"
}
```
Note: connector uses mTLS + short-lived session tokens, and we never store private key material from the customer's HSM.

infra-bot: Automated note: See playbook "Enterprise BYOK Checklist" in Confluence for required artifacts: network diagram, KMS policy, HSM vendor contact, and audit export sample.

kelly_sales (Sales): Awesome — can someone DM me the one-paragraph assurance and the POC estimate so I can send to BankCorp? Also include the connector snippet with ARNs redacted. :white_check_mark:

nina_sec (Security): DM sent with redacted snippet and assurance paragraph. Happy to join the vendor review call if they want a deep dive.

arap_se (SE): I'll be on the POC kickoff. If BankCorp asks about key-escrow or escrowed backups we can propose an air-gapped HSM export process subject to legal/ops sign-off.

kelly_sales (Sales): Thanks team — filing this into the deal thread and sending over now. If they push for cryptographic key-splitting we may need additional vendor procurement time.
